label: Product Overview
title: Product Overview
summary: Use a Product Overview to introduce one product: its picture, a chip, its name, a line of trust, and two or three key facts.
corePrinciple: One product, and the facts that matter.

anatomy.title: A picture, a chip, a name, and facts
anatomy.description: A white panel centres the product’s picture, a chip naming the metal or brand, the product’s name, a description, and a row of stats, 12 px apart.

configuration.title: Picture, chip, facts, and colour
configuration.description: imageSource adds the product’s picture at the top, fitted inside the full width at 288:170 unless imageRatio says otherwise; without it the card starts at the chip. labelImageSource puts a small round picture in the chip. stats takes any number of facts in equal columns, and [] removes the row. children adds your own content between the description and the stats, with the card’s modes. Text Appearance colours the name and the stat labels.

sizing.title: The host sets the width
sizing.description: The card fills its host’s width; Figma draws it at 343 px. The picture fills the width inside 24 px of padding, so a wider card has a taller picture, and the parts are 12 px apart. The name and description wrap. Stat values and labels stay on one line and end in … unless disableTruncation is set.

content.title: The product, its metal, and its figures
content.description: Make productName the product with its size, such as 5g Gold Coin, and the chip’s label the metal or brand, not the product again. The description is a sentence or two on why to trust it. A stat value is the figure, such as 995 or 3%, and its label a word or two, such as Purity or GST.

sources.title: Use the public Product Overview contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (19 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Product Overview has no properties; the picture, chip, text, and two stats are layers there, and the coin picture here is Figma’s own. The description’s colour token is white in every Text Appearance mode, so the description can’t be read on the white card, here and in Storybook; Figma’s is dark grey. The package’s picture fills the card’s width (Figma’s is 288 × 170, centred), and its text lines are taller, so the card is about 409 px tall where Figma’s is 396. disableTruncation affects only the stats. The published Storybook is older than the installed package and still shows the older generated page (all reported).
